rows.grounds: kvacid + ajñānin + sevita; source of service

items.question: Can service rendered by an ignorant person yield a genuine result even when truth is present?
premises: Truth may be present in some respect.
Service may be performed by an ignorant person.
No fruit is observed from such service.
items.inference: Ignorant service does not produce the intended fruit despite the presence of truth.
uncertainties: The exact scope of phala in this context is not fully specified.
items.plain_english: Even if truth is present, no fruit is seen anywhere from what is served by an ignorant person.

items.question: Wherever truth is affirmed, does it entail the nature of being the universal form?
premises: Wherever something is considered, there a corresponding status is asserted.
Truth-ness is asserted in that context.
Universal-form-ness is asserted together with it.
items.inference: Truth-ness and universal-form-ness are coextensive in every locus.
items.plain_english: Wherever and wherever, there and there, there is truth-ness and universal-form-ness.

rows.grounds: refers to the knower or supreme

items.question: Can a pot defined by formed and unformed properties fall within the range of that reality?
premises: A pot is characterized by a union of formed and unformed properties.
That reality has a certain cognitive range.
The pot is denied as falling within that range.
items.inference: The pot, as a conditioned object, is not within the range of that reality.
uncertainties: The referent of tasya is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: The pot, as a union of formed and unformed properties, is not within its range.

items.question: How can a knower cognize this pot through distinction if it lacks determinate range?
premises: A knower is the subject of cognition.
This pot would be known through distinction.
The possibility of such knowing is questioned.
items.inference: Knowledge of the pot by distinction is problematic under the stated conditions.
items.plain_english: How does the knower know, by distinction, that this is a pot?

items.question: What is the intended meaning of denying that one can know this as a pot in any way?
premises: One might claim to know this as a pot.
Such knowledge is denied in any way.
The verse states this as its meaning.
items.inference: The intended meaning is that determinate knowledge of the pot is impossible under the given view.
items.plain_english: How does one know, 'this is a pot'? One could not know it in any way — that is the meaning.

items.question: Can a determinate connection by distinction arise for unreal entities like a rabbit's horn?
premises: A rabbit's horn is an unreal example.
Connection would require determination by distinction.
Such connection is denied even there.
items.inference: Unreal entities cannot support determinate relational connection.
uncertainties: vibhaktyā may refer to grammatical or ontological distinction.
items.plain_english: In a rabbit's horn and such things, there would not even be a connection by distinction.

rows.grounds: itaḥ + api; sandhi marked in text
state of being all-auspicious or all-Śiva

items.question: Does the fitness for arising of the real establish its nature as all-Śiva?
premises: The real has fitness for arising.
From this even, all-Śiva-ness is asserted.
The arising capacity is taken as significant.
items.inference: The real's capacity for arising grounds its all-Śiva nature.
uncertainties: The exact logical force of ito'pi is compressed.
items.plain_english: Even from this, because of the real's fitness for arising, there is all-Śiva-ness.

items.question: Is the Lord himself configured in the form of the effect?
premises: The Lord is the subject.
He appears in the form of effect.
This configuration is affirmed.
items.inference: The Lord himself is manifested as the effect-form.
items.plain_english: He alone, the Lord, is configured in the form of the effect.

items.question: Does the same reality become manifest again in the specific form of a sprout as effect?
premises: The reality is considered again.
It takes the form of an effect whose nature is a sprout.
It becomes in that form.
items.inference: The same reality manifests as the sprout-shaped effect.
items.plain_english: Again, it becomes in the form of an effect whose nature is a sprout.

items.question: If manifestation of this is produced here, is that manifestation itself already real?
premises: Manifestation of this is said to be made.
The status of that manifestation is questioned.
The question asks whether it is real.
items.inference: The reality-status of manifestation itself is put into doubt.
items.plain_english: Then, if its manifestation is made here, is that manifestation itself real?

items.question: If manifestation is absent or unreal, do endlessness and the possibility of loss follow?
premises: Absence of manifestation is considered.
Unreality of manifestation is considered.
Endlessness and possibility of loss are presented as consequences.
items.inference: Denying real manifestation leads to problematic consequences like endlessness or loss.
uncertainties: The exact logical link between ānantyam and hānisaṃbhava is terse.
items.plain_english: If from absence of manifestation, then endlessness; if it is unreal, there is the possibility of loss.

items.question: Why accept a half-measure that treats the sprout as unreal while calling the effect real?
premises: The sprout and such things are considered.
One might call them unreal yet accept a real effect.
Such a compromise is challenged as inconsistent.
items.inference: An inconsistent half-position on reality and unreality should be rejected.
uncertainties: The idiom ardhajaratīya is culturally specific.
items.plain_english: Even the thing, like a sprout, would be unreal only — so let the effect be real? What is the use of this half-old compromise?

rows.grounds: sat + kriyā; real making or operation

items.question: Why must real activity not be posited everywhere else while abandoning that specific manifestation?
premises: The proposed view is rejected.
Abandoning that would require positing real activity elsewhere.
Such a shift is taken as problematic.
items.inference: One cannot coherently abandon that manifestation and relocate real activity everywhere else.
uncertainties: The referent of tāṃ is inferred from context.
items.plain_english: Not so, because having abandoned that, real activity would have to be assumed everywhere else.

rows.grounds: kartṛtā + eva + īśvara; sandhi in compound

items.question: Do the Vaiśeṣikas locate agency exclusively in the Lord rather than in the effect's manifestation?
premises: The Vaiśeṣikas hold a specific view.
Agency alone is established in the Lord.
This contrasts with other possible loci of activity.
items.inference: For the Vaiśeṣikas, agency is situated only in the Lord.
items.plain_english: For the Vaiśeṣikas, indeed, agency alone is established in the Lord.

items.question: If something illuminates both itself and another, why would another thing not be like that?
premises: Something may illuminate itself and another.
No other thing is posited as the same.
The exclusion is questioned.
items.inference: The restriction against another being similarly self-and-other illuminating is challenged.
items.plain_english: If one thing illuminates itself and another, would not another be like that? Why not?

rows.grounds: na + ekena + tulyatā; phrase as single token

items.question: Does restriction in the domain of properties prevent equality with any single thing?
premises: There is restriction in the domain of properties.
Equality with one is considered.
Such equality is denied.
items.inference: Because of restriction in the property-domain, equality with one is not established.
uncertainties: The token contains internal spacing as given.
items.plain_english: Because of restriction in the domain of properties, therefore there is no equality with one.

items.question: Is manifestation an established condition of things such that a pot is called manifest?
premises: Manifestation is established for things.
A pot is taken as an example.
The pot is called manifest.
items.inference: Manifestation is a real and established condition by which things like a pot are designated manifest.
items.plain_english: Manifestation is established for things; a pot is called manifest.

items.question: Is what is made the real thing itself rather than the production of an unreal manifestation distinct from it?
premises: What exists is made or acted upon.
A manifestation distinct from it may be posited.
Making of an unreal distinct manifestation is denied.
items.inference: Production concerns the real entity, not an unreal manifestation separate from it.
items.plain_english: What is real is made, but not the making of an unreal manifestation distinct from it.

items.question: When a lamp makes a pot manifest, is it the manifestation of what is already real that is effected?
premises: A lamp is an instrument.
Manifestation of a pot and such things is made.
The manifestation concerns what is real.
items.inference: The lamp effects manifestation of an already real object.
uncertainties: The final vā may introduce an unstated alternative.
items.plain_english: By a lamp, the manifestation of a pot and so on is made — of what is real indeed, or...

rows.grounds: by a single cause or agent

items.question: Can the unreal arise, given that one thing is not equal to another as a cause?
premises: One thing differs from another.
Arising of the unreal is considered.
Such arising is denied.
items.inference: The unreal cannot arise, even when causal differences are considered.
items.plain_english: Because of non-equality with another by one, there is not, or cannot be, the arising of the unreal.

items.question: Why can neither object nor effect arise then if their nature is mere absence?
premises: An object and an effect are under consideration.
At that time they would have the nature of absence.
Absence-nature undermines their arising.
items.inference: If object and effect are essentially absent, their arising cannot be accounted for.
items.plain_english: And because at that time the object and the effect would have the nature of absence.

items.question: Does effort arise from observing another previously seen pot as a basis for action?
premises: Another pot previously seen is observed.
Effort follows upon that observation.
The sequence links prior cognition to action.
items.inference: Effort is prompted by recognizing another instance like a previously seen pot.
uncertainties: The split surface ghaṭā[4 ] ntaraṃ reflects the given tokenization.
items.plain_english: Having observed another pot previously seen, then there is effort.

rows.grounds: kāraka + ātmatā; status as causal factor

items.question: If a sprout is said to be born, can it possess the status of a causal agent?
premises: A sprout is said to be born.
Agent-ness is considered for it.
Such agent-ness is denied.
items.inference: The sprout, as something born, does not have true causal agent-ness.
items.plain_english: If one says 'a sprout is born', there would not be agent-ness.

rows.grounds: karma + ākhya; the factor called object

items.question: How can there be a connection with the unreal if the so-called object is itself unreal?
premises: The so-called object is unreal.
A connection with that unreal is proposed.
Connection with the unreal is questioned.
items.inference: No real connection can be established with what is unreal.
uncertainties: karmākhya is taken in the grammatical-causal sense of object.
items.plain_english: Indeed, because the so-called object is unreal, how could there be a connection with the unreal?
